title: The Dogs and the Hides
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Once upon a time a number of Dogs, who were famished with hunger, saw some Hides steeping in a river, but couldn't get at them because the water was too deep. So they put their heads together, and decided to drink away at the river till it was shallow enough for them to reach the Hides. But long before that happened they burst themselves with drinking.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what condition were the Dogs in?
options: Famished with hunger
Exhausted from a long chase
Recovering from an injury
Fast asleep

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Dogs see in the river?
options: Some Hides steeping in the water
A school of fish
A fallen tree
Another pack of dogs swimming

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why couldn't the Dogs get at the Hides right away?
options: The water was too deep
The Hides were locked in a cage
Another animal was guarding them
The current was too strong

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what plan did the Dogs decide on?
options: To drink the river until it was shallow enough to reach the Hides
To dig a channel to drain the river
To wait until winter froze the river
To ask a bird to fetch the Hides for them

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the Dogs before the river became shallow enough?
options: They burst themselves with drinking
They gave up and went home
They found a shorter way around
They fell asleep by the riverbank

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "famished" mean in "famished with hunger"?
options: Extremely hungry
Very tired
Badly injured
Deeply confused

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "steeping" mean in "some Hides steeping in a river"?
options: Soaking in liquid
Floating on the surface
Burning slowly
Freezing solid

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: A reckless plan pursued without limits can destroy those who attempt it
Hides are always safer left in deep water
Dogs should never work together on a difficult task
Hunger is easily solved by patience alone

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where were the Hides located?
options: Steeping in a river
Hanging on a fence
Buried under leaves
Stacked in a barn

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Dogs do together before deciding on their plan?
options: They put their heads together
They howled at the moon
They fought over the Hides
They ran along the riverbank

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what ultimately happened to the Dogs' hunger problem?
options: It was never solved, as they burst themselves with drinking first
It was solved once they reached the Hides
It was solved when another animal shared its food
It disappeared once the river ran dry naturally

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does the idiom "put their heads together" mean in the passage?
options: They thought and planned as a group
They physically touched heads to keep warm
They argued loudly with one another
They fell asleep side by side

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what flaw led to the Dogs' downfall?
options: They pursued their goal without limit, never considering that the effort itself would harm them
They misjudged how deep the river actually was
They trusted a plan suggested by an outsider
They failed to notice the Hides were rotten

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: Hungry Dogs try to drink a river dry to reach some Hides, but ruin themselves with drinking before ever reaching the goal
Hungry Dogs successfully drink the river shallow and eat the Hides
Dogs abandon their plan to reach the Hides once they realize the river is too deep
Dogs find an easier way to cross the river and reach the Hides safely
